title: Cached remote-stream storage before explicit ownership
workload: Real g_recv/g_decode/g_force paths with queued protobuf messages containing 16-character strings; 1/32/128 elements, complete consumption, stopping after half, and retaining the first position. Every consumed position is read twice.
comparison: Existing fwp runtime across input sizes and consumption patterns, not an alternative implementation or C/Rust speed comparison.
measurement: O2, collection/stress/verification disabled; setup and receive allocations separated. Charged bytes include allocator size rounding. Raw queued messages and codec scratch are excluded from charged managed bytes; unread-message count is recorded. Library shutdown releases every queued message.
results: Four managed requests and 89 requested bytes per received value, charging 112 bytes. Setup charges 688 bytes. Clearing C roots does not release this storage; cells still depend on tracing or whole-library teardown.
limits: Not end-to-end networking, connection-pool behavior, elapsed time, total process memory or proof of explicit ownership. C roots are cleared without inventing a release operation the runtime does not yet provide.
checks: O1/O2 semantic agreement with known decoded strings, stress and verification enabled/disabled
Repeated forcing returns the cached value without another allocation or receive
Retained first position survives later consumption
Library shutdown frees every queued message
Deliberately removing the forced-cell cache check exits with the expected failure status 34
